overview.description: Chicago Poker is a Seven Card Stud variant where the pot is split between the highest poker hand and the player holding the highest (or lowest) spade in the hole. Face-up spades do not count—only concealed spades are eligible. This creates a unique dual-objective game where players must balance traditional poker hand strength with the hunt for hidden spades.

history.origins: Chicago Poker emerged in American home games as a Seven Card Stud variant, likely in the mid-20th century. The game gained popularity as a 'Dealer's Choice' option due to its exciting split-pot mechanic and the added suspense of hunting for spades in the hole.
timeline: 1950s: Seven Card Stud variants with split pots become popular in American home games.
1960s-70s: Chicago (High Chicago) emerges as a distinct variant with the spade-in-hole mechanic.
1980s: Low Chicago variant gains popularity as an alternative scoring option.
1990s-Present: Remains a staple of home poker games and Dealer's Choice rotations; rarely found in casinos.
history.evolution: The game spawned numerous related variants including Follow the Queen (wild cards determined by queens), Dirty Schultz (wilds from pairs), and The Bitch (Queen of Spades penalty). The core spade-in-hole mechanic has remained consistent across all Chicago variants.
history.cultural: Primarily played in home games and social poker settings. The game is valued for creating action and keeping more players in the hand due to the split pot possibility.

setup.equipment: Standard deck, poker chips, dealer button.
setup.dealing: Seven Card Stud format: 2 cards face down, 4 cards face up, 1 card face down. Five betting rounds total.

rules.objective: Win half the pot with the highest poker hand OR win half the pot by holding the highest spade in the hole (face-down cards only).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Ante**: All players post an ante. 2. **Initial Deal**: Each player receives 2 cards face down and 1 card face up. 3. **Bring-in**: Player with the lowest upcard posts a compulsory bring-in bet (or highest in some variants). 4. **Betting Rounds**: Five rounds of betting follow each card dealt (after 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th streets). 5. **Declaration**: After final betting, active players declare whether they are going for High Hand, High Spade, or Both.
keyRules: Pot is split 50/50 between best poker hand and highest spade in the hole (High Chicago).
Only FACE-DOWN spades count for the spade half of the pot.
If the Ace of Spades is dealt face up, the King of Spades in the hole becomes the best possible spade.
Declaration can be sequential (around the table) or simultaneous (chips in fist: 1=High Hand, 2=High Spade, 3=Both).
To win the spade half, you MUST have a spade face down. Without one, you cannot win that half even if no one else declares spade.
Declaring 'Both' requires winning BOTH halves to win anything (Pig Rule in some variants).

strategy.basic: Watch the upcards carefully. If you see the Ace, King, and Queen of Spades all dealt face up, your Jack of Spades in the hole becomes much more valuable. Conversely, if high spades are showing, your hole spade is less likely to win.
strategy.intermediate: Balanced Play: If you have a strong poker hand but no spade in the hole, you can only win half the pot. Consider whether your hand is strong enough to justify playing for half. If you have a weak hand but the Ace of Spades in the hole, you have a lock on half the pot and should stay in.
strategy.advanced: Declaration Strategy: In simultaneous declaration games, watch your opponents' betting patterns. Heavy betting often indicates a strong poker hand; cautious play with many spades showing might indicate someone hunting for the spade half. If you have both a strong hand AND a high spade, declaring 'Both' can scoop the entire pot—but you must win both halves.
tips: Track all spades: Count how many spades are visible and which ranks remain possible in holes.
The Ace of Spades in the hole is the 'nuts' for the spade half—it's unbeatable.
If four or more spades are showing on board, the remaining spades in holes are more valuable.
Don't overvalue medium-strength poker hands when you have no spade—you can only win half.
In Low Chicago, the Two of Spades in the hole is the nuts (aces count high).

list.name: Low Chicago
list.description: Pot splits between highest hand and LOWEST spade in the hole (Ace counts high). Best hole spade is 2♠, worst is A♠.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Same engine as base; only spade half ranking differs (low instead of high).

list.name: San Francisco
list.description: Same as Chicago but using Hearts instead of Spades. High San Francisco = highest heart in hole; Low San Francisco = lowest heart in hole.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Same engine as base; suit for hole-card half changes from spades to hearts.

list.name: Follow the Queen
list.description: When a Queen is dealt face up, the next card dealt becomes wild for all players, as do all other cards of that rank. If another Queen appears, the wild card changes.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Wild-card variant; overrides needed when wild logic is added to engine.

list.name: Dirty Schultz
list.description: Similar to Follow the Queen, but wild cards are determined when any player shows a natural pair face up. The next card dealt becomes wild.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Wild-card variant; overrides needed when wild logic is added to engine.

list.name: The Bitch
list.description: If the Queen of Spades is dealt face up, the hand ends immediately. Cards are reshuffled and redealt to players who hadn't folded.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Hand-end condition variant; overrides needed for early-termination logic.

list.name: Black Mariah
list.description: Multiple variants exist: sometimes synonymous with The Bitch, sometimes a version where you need both best hand AND highest spade to win.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Multiple interpretations; overrides depend on which variant is implemented.

difficulty.easy: Ignores spade tracking; plays only for poker hand value; makes random declarations.
difficulty.medium: Tracks visible spades and calculates probability of hole spades; makes reasonable declarations based on hand strength and spade holdings.
difficulty.hard: Perfect spade counting; optimal declaration timing; understands implied odds of split pots; can execute sophisticated bluffs representing spade strength.

considerations: AI must track all 13 spades and determine which are still possible in holes.
Declaration phase requires game theory optimal play based on hand strength and spade probability.
Split pot dynamics change pot odds calculations significantly.
In variants with wild cards, AI must adjust hand strength calculations dynamically.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Seven Card Stud variant where the pot splits between the highest hand and the highest spade in the hole.

prompts.human: Welcome to Chicago Poker! This Seven Card Stud variant splits the pot—half to the best hand, half to the highest SPADE IN THE HOLE. Face-up spades don't count! Watch your opponents' upcards to track which spades might still be hidden. Can you balance building a strong hand with hunting for that Ace of Spades in the hole
prompts.ai: Game: Chicago Poker. Seven Card Stud, split pot. 2-8 players. 2 down, 1 up; 4th-6th up, 7th down. Five betting rounds. Pot splits 50/50: best 5-card hand wins half, highest face-down spade wins half. Must have spade in hole to win spade half. Variants: Low Chicago (lowest spade), Follow the Queen, etc.

scoring.description: High-Low Split pot. 50% to the best poker hand, 50% to the highest spade in the hole (High Chicago) or lowest spade in the hole (Low Chicago).
scoring.winCondition: Highest poker rank wins the high half; highest (or lowest) qualifying spade in hole wins the spade half.
scoring.splitRules: Pot is split 50/50 between best poker hand and best hole spade. One player can win both halves if they have both the best hand and the best hole spade. Odd chips go to the high hand winner.
